D11·ef4a — 2026-09-16
rule: A conformance or perf target names its TypeScript commit; a re-record states the sha and a reason per changed golden, and keeps the previous set alongside.
chose: Both parity targets are pinned to a NAMED COMMIT of the TypeScript engine, never a branch tip: the perf baseline records the sha of the build it measured (`commit` in baseline.typescript.json; a45ea21 on r1-fixes for the first fixed target) and the conformance goldens, when re-recorded, carry a manifest naming the sha they were recorded from plus a one-line reason per golden that changed. The target moves only deliberately, by a Decision; the final target is the r1-fixes RC commit round 2 runs (bench-refresh D20). The 0.32.0 as-shipped goldens are kept alongside the re-recorded set so the RC's intentional digest changes stay auditable, exactly as the as-shipped perf baseline is.
over: Recording against whatever the r1-fixes tip is when a session happens to run; letting a re-record replace goldens with no per-file reason.
because: The r1-fixes tip changed digest bytes in 16 of 27 goldens for reasons unrelated to 2.7; a target that follows a moving branch would let an unintended TypeScript behaviour change be absorbed silently as "new expected", which D2 forbids. Proposed by the r1-fixes session (sofar-4c) 2026-09-16 and adopted here; the golden manifest is built at the re-record that follows the rebase onto r1-fixes.
